Action Plan:
1. Acute diarrhoea / suspected gastroenteritis:
   • Encourage liberal oral fluids; purchase oral re-hydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte) and take as directed.  
   • Symptomatic relief: paracetamol 2 tablets up to four times daily (dose/route/frequency not fully documented).  
   • Rest at home and refrain from work for the next 2–3 days.  
   • Safety-net: if diarrhoea lasts >3–4 days, if blood appears in stool/vomit, high fever, or signs of dehydration develop, arrange urgent review; stool culture may be required at that stage.
2. Follow-up: telephone or in-person review if no improvement in 3–4 days or sooner if deterioration.
3. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for call: 3-day history of frequent loose watery stools.  
• History of presenting illness  
  – Onset: symptoms began 3 days ago, ~24 h after eating Chinese takeaway.  
  – Frequency: 6–7 bowel motions/day.  
  – Character: watery, no blood or mucus.  
  – Associated symptoms: intermittent cramp-like left-lower-abdominal pain, initial vomiting (now settled), subjective fever at onset, weakness/shakiness, loss of appetite; able to tolerate fluids.  
  – No night sweats, no persistent vomiting, no radiation of pain, no back pain.  
• Past medical history: well-controlled asthma.  
• Medications: inhaler (type, dose, frequency not documented); no other regular medicines.  
• Allergies: not documented.  
• Social history: married, lives with wife and 2 children (one child vomited once, no diarrhoea); accountant; non-smoker; does not consume alcohol.  
• Recent exposure: Chinese restaurant meal 4 days ago; no similar illness in family except child’s brief vomiting.

Objective:
• Teleconsultation — physical examination not performed, no vital signs available.  
• No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhoea / possible infectious gastroenteritis  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute viral gastroenteritis (DDx: “Acute viral gastroenteritis” – High).  
   - Differential diagnosis:  
     • Acute bacterial food-borne infection (Medium) – possible given takeaway meal; no blood or household clustering (opposes).  
     • Diverticulitis with secondary diarrhoea (Low–Medium) – less likely; pain intermittent, large-volume stools, younger age.  
     • Inflammatory bowel disease flare (Low) – unlikely given acute onset and absence of blood.  
   - Investigations planned: none immediately; stool culture considered if symptoms persist >3–4 days or worsen.  
   - Treatment: oral hydration, oral re-hydration solution (Dioralyte), paracetamol for fever/pain, rest, 2–3 days off work.  
   - Referrals: none at present.

2. Asthma (background)  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Stable, well-controlled asthma (no acute issue).  
   - Differential diagnosis: not applicable.  
   - Investigations planned: none.  
   - Treatment: continue inhaler as usual.  
   - Referrals: none.

Quality checks:
● Missing data: allergies not elicited; brand/type and regimen for inhaler not documented; no vital signs or physical examination; no medication reconciliation beyond inhaler.  
● No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; minimal background noise.
